meditations.title: Meditations: a map of ideas
meditations.description: Marcus Aurelius's private notes, in George Long's public-domain translation: twelve books across, five recurring ideas down. Every box is his wording, with its book and section.

themes.label: Do the work in front of you

themes.label: Other people
passages: From my grandfather Verus [I learned] good morals and the government of my temper.

themes.label: It's your judgment that hurts
passages: The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
Take away thy opinion, and then there is taken away the complaint, "I have been harmed."
Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgment about it.

themes.label: Only the present is yours
passages: the present is the only thing of which a man can be deprived

Do not disturb thyself by thinking of the whole of thy life.

themes.label: You will die, and be forgotten
passages: Since it is possible that thou mayest depart from life this very moment, regulate every act and thought accordingly.
Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years.

odyssey.title: The Odyssey: a story map
odyssey.description: Homer's story in Samuel Butler's public-domain translation, which uses Roman names (Ulysses, Minerva). The poem tells it out of order; the arrows show how the pieces join. Every line is Butler's, with its book.
